name: Zohran Mamdani
role: Mayor of New York City (2026–); member of the New York State Assembly (2021–2025)
summary: A Democratic Socialists of America member and Democrat who emphasizes affordability: a rent freeze, fare-free buses, universal child care, a $30 minimum wage and higher taxes on high earners and corporations. He favors a civilian community-safety agency alongside a retained NYPD, sanctuary protections for immigrants, LGBTQ and reproductive rights, and public renewable power. He is a prominent critic of Israeli policy, supporting BDS and ICC warrants, while saying Israel has a right to exist with equal rights for all.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Supports the New York Health Act (single-payer).

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Platform calls for a $30 minimum wage by 2030.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Proposes city-run grocery stores, a rent freeze and free buses, implying public provision beats markets in these areas; not stated as a general claim.

public-ownership.rationale: Cosponsored the Build Public Renewables Act (public power authority) and sponsored public-utility bills; no stated stance on rail or all major industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed raising the corporate rate to 11.5% and a 2% surcharge on incomes over $1 million; said he does not think billionaires should exist.

unions-good.rationale: Pledged in his victory speech to stand alongside unions and expand labor protections; backs union labor on public projects.

property-fundamental.rationale: Proposes that the city take over buildings of serial code violators and give them to tenants, and supports rent freezes and stronger rent control.

regulate-corporations.rationale: As mayor ordered the consumer protection agency to pursue hidden junk fees and subscription traps, saying companies must be held to account.

cut-welfare.rationale: Record and platform expand public programs (child care, groceries, housing); no support for cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Sponsored a 2024 Assembly bill making worker cooperatives and employee-owned firms preferred contractors for state contracts.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Said the city can be kept safe while respecting rights, rejected suspicion based on religion, and said he supports the Handschu limits on NYPD surveillance.

state-harmful.rationale: Argues for public excellence and a stronger public sector.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted for multiple Assembly gun-control bills, tweeted in 2022 'We need to ban all guns', and in 2025 called for tougher national assault-rifle laws.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said he does not want more officers and the NYPD's size is appropriate; proposed a civilian Community Safety department and abolishing the Strategic Response Group; kept the commissioner.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Cosponsored legislation in the Assembly to decriminalize sex work, though he has not emphasized it and said he would not prioritize it as mayor.

decide-locally.rationale: Sponsored bills to let localities set their own minimum wage and fare-free buses, but backs state single-payer healthcare and national assault-rifle limits.

rehabilitation.rationale: Committed to closing Rikers, ordered solitary confinement compliance and opened therapeutic housing; appointed a formerly incarcerated corrections commissioner.

abortion-legal.rationale: Backed Proposal 1 (2024) protecting reproductive rights in the state constitution.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Signed a pledge to champion reparations as mayor and said New York was 'very complicit' in slavery and that acknowledging it matters.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His sanctuary-city record is about how immigrants are treated, not how many should come; no statement on national immigration levels was found.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Treats climate action as central; cosponsored Build Public Renewables Act; backs All-Electric Buildings Act and congestion pricing.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Asked in the October 2025 debate whether he backs new nuclear plants, called it 'something worth exploring' and answered 'Yeah' when asked if that was a yes.

one-party-rule.rationale: His campaign said Maduro and Díaz-Canel are dictators whose governments stifled free and fair elections and jailed opponents, though he avoided the word in the interview itself.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said after the Charlie Kirk killing that political violence has no place in the United States, and calls its normalization terrifying.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Criticized the 'reckless adoption of technology', banned generative AI in lower grades and backed a data center moratorium.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Reportedly said his focus 'is on outcomes' when reversing on mayoral control, though he calls himself a democratic socialist.

direct-action.rationale: Joined a 2021 taxi-driver hunger strike and was arrested at a protest blocking traffic, yet he has pursued his programme mainly through elected office.

taxation-theft.rationale: Proposes tax increases on corporations and millionaires to fund public services and treats taxation as the way to pay for universal programs.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Says Israel has a right to exist 'as a state with equal rights' but, asked again in June 2026, would not support it as a Jewish state because it privileges one religion.

force-without-un.rationale: Called the January 2026 US strike on Venezuela an act of war violating federal and international law, and called for an end to the US war with Iran.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposed the Astoria gas peaker plant and backed public renewables.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His platform adds fare-free buses, free child care from six weeks to five years and city-owned grocery stores, functions far beyond defence, justice and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Opposes racism and supports LGBTQ, immigrant and Muslim New Yorkers' equal standing.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: He explicitly supported a statewide rent supplement for households facing eviction or homelessness (2022 questionnaire, question 42). His 2026 housing plan preserves and expands housing for tenants alongside homeownership, and he expressly defends provision for future tenants; these positions support continued renting rather than requiring every family to own its home.

religious-exemptions.rationale: An earlier pass reported a remark protecting Hasidic yeshivas from education-standard enforcement, but only Wikipedia and opinion columns report it; no verifiable source found.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: His calls to end the occupation of Palestinian territory and his opposition to Russia's invasion of Ukraine are not statements about annexed territory as such; no recorded position on annexation found.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Proposed a new 2% city income tax only on incomes over $1 million, a rate that rises with income.

corporate-influence.rationale: Speech rejects politics that answers to the few and criticizes billionaires avoiding taxes; lobbying and campaign money not specifically addressed.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Says the city should comply with international law and that Netanyahu belongs in The Hague, but also that he will act on the ICC warrant only as far as New York law allows; the evidence points both ways.

religious-nation.rationale: Rejects any state that privileges one religion and says everyone should be considered equal whatever their faith, describing equal rights as the bedrock of being American.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Criticizes governments that 'hollow out' capacity and privatize responsibilities as costing more, but his city grocery stores will be run by a private operator.

socialized-care.rationale: Proposes universal public child care; says nothing on housework being socialized.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Marked Yom HaShoah by honouring 'the six million Jewish victims of the Nazis' systematic program of mass murder'.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Strong record of LGBTQ rights support.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned Iran's government for systematic repression and for killing thousands who sought to express dissent, and faulted Maduro and Díaz-Canel for jailing political opponents.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said politics should no longer be done to people; proposed co-governance of schools with parent councils.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Backed Proposal 1 on gender identity protections, supports gender-affirming care, created an Office of LGBTQIA+ Affairs.

assisted-dying.rationale: Cosponsored the Medical Aid in Dying Act, which passed the legislature in 2025.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Himself Muslim; said New York will no longer be a place where one can traffic in Islamophobia and win.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said he does not think there should be billionaires given inequality and rejected politics that answers only to the few.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Backed defunding in a 2020 tweet but as candidate and mayor kept the NYPD and moved away from defund rhetoric; wants Rikers closed but not prisons abolished.

rent-control.rationale: Supports rent control and froze rents on rent-stabilized units (Rent Guidelines Board two-year freeze, 2026).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Commemorated the Armenian genocide in 2026 and condemned the Nagorno-Karabakh expulsions; also calls Gaza a genocide.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Backs fare-free public buses and public renewable power; water and hospitals not addressed.

dense-cities.rationale: Backs increased density near transit and congestion pricing.

free-public-college.rationale: Proposes tuition-free CUNY and SUNY funded by a tax on the wealthy and sponsored bills for free SUNY tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Supports congestion pricing, kept it in the 2025 debate, and co-introduced a weight-based vehicle registration fee bill.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Backs unions and his administration reached labor settlements with delivery-app platforms; no explicit statement on bargaining versus individual contracts.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Said Netanyahu 'belongs in The Hague' as a leader charged by the International Criminal Court, and that anybody the ICC has called for should be honoured.

national-church-status.rationale: Told ABC that he cannot support any state that privileges one religion over another, whether Israel, Saudi Arabia or anywhere else, because people should be equal whatever their faith.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Flagship programs (free buses, universal child care) are universal rather than limited to the poorest.

notes:
Born October 18, 1991; living. Positions have shifted in office: he reversed his opposition to mayoral control of schools, retreated from 'defund the police' rhetoric, and later dropped some earlier stances (SHSAT). Most evidence on specific issues comes from secondary reports; positions not directly documented are left null.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 23 answers taken from it, 28 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Shifts: in 2020 he voiced support for defunding the NYPD and called it racist; as a candidate and mayor he said he would work with police, apologized for the earlier remark, kept Commissioner Tisch and still pursues disbanding the Strategic Response Group and a Department of Community Safety. He campaigned to end mayoral control of schools but lobbied for a two-year extension as mayor. City grocery stores were first proposed as city-run and then to be run by a private operator. On Israel he has said it has a right to exist but will not endorse it as a Jewish state, and he supports a permanent ceasefire, an end to occupation and equal rights for all. DSA platform planks (for example leaving NATO) were not counted because he said his positions are the ones he states himself. Government (elections, courts, executive power) and several world topics (Ukraine, NATO, trade, aid) remain thin because he has not spoken to them in sources found.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-10-31), aimed at line 13 (nationalism, irredentism, supranational union). Searched his interviews (NYT The Interview, Jon Stewart, Odd Lots, Hasan Piker, ABC This Week June 2026, CBS 100-day interview, 9/11 interview), the three mayoral debates and the victory speech (captions downloaded and searched), plus the web, for: pan-national or civilizational unity (pan-African, Muslim world), the EU or pooled sovereignty, territorial claims and reunification (Kashmir, Ukraine and Crimea, Greenland), territorial expansion, an anti-Western front or the Global South, land redistribution, national rebirth, a third way between capitalism and communism, settler colonialism, the Palestinian right of return, colonial reparations (only a remark about the Kohinoor diamond, which is not reparations), immigration levels and open borders. None of these has a stated position: line 13 statements stay null. Added: ICC trials (+2), national church status (-1) and a religiously defined nation (-1). Reviewed the world answers: annexed-territory-occupation set to null (occupation and the Ukraine invasion are not annexation), national-law-over-international lowered to 0 (he backs the ICC warrant but says he will act only within New York law), force-without-un re-sourced from Wikipedia to City & State and his interview. Nine answers that rested only on Wikipedia were re-sourced to the reports or documents behind them (regulate-corporations, worker-ownership, one-party-rule (lowered to -1), suppress-opposition, direct-action, night-watchman-state, flat-income-tax, holocaust-denial); religious-exemptions became null for lack of a verifiable source. claude-haiku-5-5 cheap pass (2026-10-31), line 13: searched noncitizen voting in local elections (no statement; the city law was struck down), a city-owned bank (co-sponsored A3352 and pledged a city bank in the victory speech, but a public bank is not a bank owned by its users at cost), city-run grocery stores (a narrow case, not the general statement on public ownership of means of production or on markets), AI and technological progress (no claim that progress will solve problems), and guaranteed income (nothing found). None gives a stated position on the line 13 statements, so they stay null. gpt-6 pass (2026-10-31, Codex; exact runtime version not exposed), line 13 only: Read all 52 supplied statements, the existing audit and earlier-pass notes, the local source-library index and relevant passages in its interviews and debates; checked the local corpus inventory. Targeted web searches covered Palestinian refugee return, noncitizen local voting, religious exemptions including vaccination, pooled sovereignty and the EU, common currency and pan-African unity or reunification, intellectual property, land redistribution, guaranteed income, markets and cooperative ownership, central planning, the UN and term limits. No further statement was settled by his own words or record: the Nakba-video article inferred support for return from commemoration and a guest's account, not his stated position on return including descendants; statewide term limits do not settle presidential reelection; public banks, groceries and cooperative advocacy do not settle the broader ownership claims. A full housing-plan PDF was blocked; a GitHub mirror search found only a link, so the housing answer uses the opened official release and his questionnaire. Remaining statements had no matching evidence.
